comparisons.title: 1Password vs Bitwarden (2026): The Verdict, Verified Prices, and Who Should Buy Which
comparisons.meta_description: 1Password vs Bitwarden, decided: verified 2026 pricing on both sides, the honest trade-off (polish vs value), choose-if lists for each, and the tiebreaker when both fit.
comparisons.quick_verdict: Buy 1Password if a refined, effortless experience for you or your family justifies paying roughly $28–47 more per year than Bitwarden Premium. Buy Bitwarden if you lead with value, want a genuinely unlimited free tier, or require open source and self-hosting. Both use zero-knowledge encryption and are safe, reputable choices — this is a values decision, not a safety decision.
comparisons.best_for_a: Households and professionals who want the most polished apps, best family sharing UX, and features like Travel Mode — and consider experience worth $3.99/mo (verified regular price; $2.99 first-year promo).
comparisons.best_for_b: Budget-conscious users (including 'free'), open-source advocates, self-hosters, and families who want 6 premium accounts for $3.99/mo total ($0.67/person at capacity).
choose_a_if: You'll pay for polish: 1Password's apps, autofill, and organization are the category benchmark
Family sharing is central — unlimited shared vaults with the smoothest admin and recovery UX
You want Watchtower's proactive security guidance and Travel Mode
You're a new customer — the verified first-year promo ($2.99 Individual / $4.49 Families) softens year one
You prefer not to think about billing terms: one annual plan, transparent regular pricing
choose_b_if: Price is the constraint: free forever, or $19.80/yr for Premium (both verified)
You want open-source code, self-hosting, or a US/EU-hosted, audit-friendly stack
Your household is up to 6 people — Families covers 6 premium accounts at $3.99/mo total
You want an integrated TOTP authenticator without paying 1Password prices
You're advising a mixed group: Bitwarden's free tier means nobody is priced out of basic security
comparisons.key_difference: You are choosing between experience and leverage. 1Password sells the best-finished product in the category at $47.88/yr (Individual, regular). Bitwarden gives the security fundamentals away free and sells convenience for $19.80/yr. Neither has a meaningful security-quality advantage for typical users; the difference is app polish, family UX, business tooling — and price.

comparisons.tiebreaker: If both fit your budget and needs, let two questions decide. (1) Who is this for? Families who want zero friction → 1Password; mixed groups or budget-shared households → Bitwarden. (2) What annoys you more: paying ~$28/yr more for a better product, or occasionally clunkier software? Your honest answer is the verdict. You can also run both trials — 1Password's 14-day trial and Bitwarden's free tier make this the rare decision you can test before making.
comparisons.use_cases_note: Families: our dedicated use-case page runs the per-person math and recovery comparison. Free-first shoppers: the free-vs-paid guide. Enterprise buyers: verify current business quotes directly with both vendors; we did not verify business pricing on 1Password's side.

faqs.a: Not meaningfully for typical users. Both use zero-knowledge AES-256 encryption. 1Password adds a Secret Key (a second secret), Bitwarden offers open-source verifiability and self-hosting. Choose on experience and price, not safety.

faqs.q: Can I switch from one to the other easily?
faqs.a: Yes — both support standard CSV export/import, and Bitwarden documents direct imports from 1Password. Budget an hour, change your master password everywhere after moving, and keep the old export encrypted while you verify.
For experience: 1Password (unlimited shared vaults, smooth recovery). For value: Bitwarden (6 premium accounts for $3.99/mo total). The full per-person math is in our families use-case page.

faqs.q: Which has the better free version?
faqs.a: Bitwarden — 1Password has no free tier. Bitwarden Free is unlimited in passwords and devices, verified on the official pricing page in September 2026.
